text:
Sara: quick sync — design question: how do we want canary/A-B rollouts to trigger automatic fallback across Hosted / Dedicated / Private? thinking about a single policy engine vs per-deploy adapters
Miguel: +1 need one control plane but different enforcement paths for private stacks
Deepa: agree. policy engine should emit intents (eg: route-weight, model-variant, degrade-mode) not direct actions
Tara: important: private deployments can't call central control plane during outage. we need local policy adapters that can run in offline mode
Jon: proposal: central policy -> serialize signed policy blob -> adapters periodically pull and validate. adapters enforce locally (and can fallback to defaults)
Sara: sounds good. what are the failure signals that should trigger fallback?
Miguel: shortlist: error-rate spikes, 95/99p latency breaches, increased token-cost anomalies, quality regressions from eval hooks, resource OOMs
Deepa: also probe failures from healthcheck pool and slow KV cache warmups (if prefix cache cold then latency jumps)
Sara: fallback targets: lower-cost model variant, smaller sequence-length cap, reduce batch size, or route to sync non-LLM fallback. order matters
Jon: +1. we should prefer graceful degrade (reduce context) before switching model family to avoid quality cliffs
Tara: for private we must expose knobs to ops: prefer-model-allowlist, local-cached-weights, force-fallback-to-offline-endpoint
Miguel: example policy blob (pseudo):
```
version: 1
match: [route: "chat.*"]
when: {error_rate>2%, p99_latency>1.2s, probe_failures>3}
action: {type: prioritized_fallback, fallbacks: [small-quant, limit-context(512), sync-api], ttl: 300}
```
Sara: policy TTL and cooldowns are critical. avoid flip-flopping: cooldown should be > rollback detect window
Deepa: also track signal confidence (use sliding window + spectrum of metrics). only cascade to heavier actions when confidence > 0.8
ops-bot: Deploy started: canary rollout 0.04 -> 0.25 for model redwood-alpha in prod-region-2 (by Miguel)
Miguel: note: canary weight ramping should respect downstream cache priming. ramp in steps with warmup hold (eg: 5m)
Jon: open question: who owns the decision to bypass canary and immediately fallback? oncall or automation?
Tara: automation first, oncall notified. require manual override for global destructive actions (eg full cutover to sync-api)
Deepa: metrics contracts: canary must emit a contract snapshot at start (p95 latency baseline, token-cost baseline, quality tests). fallback rules compare against baseline
Sara: instrumentation: need per-route fine-grained traces & token-level latency, and a small evaluation harness that runs sample prompts through canary model for quality smoke tests
Miguel: for Dedicated: adapter should also be able to throttle GPU queues and reduce batch compiler aggressiveness as a mitigation step
Jon: failure isolation: a canary fallback should expose reasons in routing decisions (eg fallback_reason=high_p99_cache) so SRE can triage faster
Sara: logging: policy decisions, signal windows, and execution trace should be emitted to Console with correlation id
Deepa: test plan: unit tests for policy engine, integration tests with an adapter emulator, and chaos tests that kill KV/cache and spike latency to validate fallback path
Tara: docs: runbook for oncall with quick commands to force-fallback, inspect policy blobs, and revoke signed blobs
Miguel: follow-up: I'll spin up a short RFC PR with sequence diagrams + policy schema and adapter API. can we aim for review this week?
Sara: yes. thanks all. tagging followups: @Deepa please draft the metric contract schema, @Tara write runbook skeleton, @Jon add routing header for fallback_reason
CI-Bot: created issue #1453: canary-fallback-policy-schema (assigned: Miguel)
Sara: end-to-end checklist later but this is a solid start :thumbsup:
